titulo: The WebMCP Readiness diagnosis: run it and read it without falling for "high score = ranking"
lead: WebMCP Readiness is INEMA's open scanner: it opens the page in an isolated browser, only reads, and returns a score in four categories. In this lesson you run the scanner on your machine, with a pinned version, against the example page and against your own site, and you learn to read the result as a diagnosis, not as a promise of ranking.
objetivo: run WebMCP Readiness on your machine and read the diagnosis without confusing score with ranking.

aprende.t: The open scanner, cloned with a pinned version
Four categories and the overall score
Expected failures and failures to fix right away
What the score doesn't tell you

hero_alt: Dark workbench with an abstract diagnostic-panel monitor and a multimeter's probe tips touching a connector.

secoes.titulo: From the page to the fix plan

nos.detalhe: The scan goes deep only on the URL you give it. The sitemap is inventoried, but the other pages are not opened in this mode.

Opens the page in a headless Chromium, reads HTML, headers, robots.txt, sitemap.xml and llms.txt, and lists the WebMCP tools with getTools() when the API exists. It doesn't run any of the site's tools.

WebMCP, SEO, GEO and AEO, each from 0 to 100. In the code of version 2.2.2, the overall score weighs 30% WebMCP, 30% SEO, 20% GEO and 20% AEO. How to read the weights in depth is the agent-ready lesson of the inemaSEO Program.
The failures and warnings with a recommendation, sorted by priority. This is what goes into the lesson 8 plan, not the score.

secoes.legenda: In the scanner's own words: SEO, GEO and AEO measure observable signals; they do not guarantee indexing, ranking or citation by AI systems.

secoes.titulo: Install the scanner with a pinned version
secoes.sub: Clone the public inematds/webmcp-readiness repository into a practice folder, pin commit 3f3d1c8 (version 2.2.2, from 09/24/2026), install the dependencies, and run its tests.

blocos.conteudo:
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-formacao-webmcp-base-v72
mkdir -p $E && cd $E
[ -d webmcp-readiness ] || git clone -q https://github.com/inematds/webmcp-readiness
cd webmcp-readiness && git checkout -q 3f3d1c8 && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --silent
npm test 2>&1 | grep -E '^ℹ (tests|pass|fail) '

abas.html:
ℹ tests 33
ℹ pass 33
ℹ fail 0

The scanner's own 33 tests pass. If the number is different, you are not on the pinned commit.

Without the scanner's dependencies installed, Node can't find @sparticuz/chromium and stops at the import. Run the whole block: npm ci is part of it.

secoes.titulo: The scanner against the example page
secoes.sub: readiness-local.mjs imports the scanner, points it to the kit's Chromium, and, only for the page at 127.0.0.1, allows the local address (the scanner blocks private networks by default).

blocos.conteudo:
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-formacao-webmcp-base-v72
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-base-v72/kit
for p in antes depois; do node readiness-local.mjs $E/webmcp-readiness $p; echo "saída: $?"; done

Clearing the 10 problems in the tree raised the score from only 48 to 52. Readiness measures other things (description, canonical, WebMCP tools); you check the tree with arvore.mjs. The three WebMCP failures are expected: the page doesn't register tools, and that is course 2.

secoes.titulo: The scanner on a real site
secoes.sub: The same command against inema.club, which belongs to INEMA and registers WebMCP tools with an origin trial token. --json saves the full report.

abas.html:
Readiness 2.2.2 · https://www.inema.club/ · nota 92 (Estrutura forte)
  WebMCP 95 · SEO 100 · GEO 88 · AEO 77
  falhas: 0 · avisos: 4 · ok: 26 · ferramentas WebMCP: 8 · document.modelContext no Chromium do scan: sim
  lembrete do próprio scanner: SEO, GEO e AEO medem sinais observáveis; não garantem indexação, ranking ou citação por sistemas de IA.
saída: 0

Score 92 with 8 tools discovered at runtime, because the kit's Chromium 153 is within the origin trial range. A high score means signals are present; it doesn't mean a search engine or an AI will cite the site.

secoes.sub: Scanner installed, the example, and your site.

exercicios.titulo: E1 · Scanner with a pinned version
exercicios.pronto: the output shows ℹ tests 33, ℹ pass 33 and ℹ fail 0.

exercicios.titulo: E2 · Before and after in the scanner
exercicios.texto: Run the "before and after" block and compare the categories. Explain, in one sentence, why the score barely changed.
exercicios.pronto: both lines start with Readiness 2.2.2, the depois.html one shows nota 52, and your sentence mentions what Readiness measures that arvore.mjs does not.

exercicios.texto: Run the template against your site's main page. Pick the three failures or warnings to handle first and say why. WebMCP tool failures with no registered tool are expected.
exercicios.pronto: the file ~/readiness-[your-site].json exists, the output ends with saída: 0, and the plan has the score with a date and the three choices.

perguntas.p: Does Readiness run a site's WebMCP tools to test them?
opcoes: Yes, it runs all the tools with test data
No: it is passive; it only lists them with getTools()
It only runs the ones marked readOnlyHint
It only runs them when the site has an MCP server
perguntas.explica: The scanner only reads. Running a site's tool is an action with consequences, and it doesn't do that.

perguntas.p: Your site scored 92. What does that score guarantee?
opcoes: That the site shows up in AI search answers
That Google moves the site up in the rankings next month
That WebMCP works in every visitor's browser
That the signals being looked for are on the page
perguntas.explica: The report itself warns: SEO, GEO and AEO don't guarantee indexing, ranking or citation. The score is a diagnosis.

perguntas.p: depois.html cleared the tree check, but the score went up only 4 points. Why?
opcoes: Because Readiness measures other things besides the tree
Because the scanner can't open local pages
Because the accessibility tree doesn't matter to agents
Because the kit's Chromium is too old for the scanner
perguntas.explica: Different tools measure different things. The tree matters to whoever operates the screen; Readiness measures SEO, GEO, AEO, and WebMCP signals.

perguntas.p: Why pin commit 3f3d1c8 instead of using the newest version?
opcoes: Because the new version of the scanner is paid
Because the new commit doesn't run on Linux or Mac
So the output matches the course's output
To avoid the Chrome origin trial during the scan
perguntas.explica: A pinned version makes "done when" verifiable. After the course, update knowing that rules and scores may change.

itens.texto: The scanner only reads; you run it on your own machine, with a pinned version.
The plan comes from the failures by priority, not from the score.

itens.t: A score is not a ranking
itens.texto: Signals being present don't guarantee a citation or a position.
